answer: An identity must be at least 6 epochs old on the quill ledger before its answer counts toward quorum, which makes fresh keys useless at the moment they are cheapest to mint. Because the age is read from the horizon checkpoint rather than self-declared, the thread audit can recompute it and a backdated claim fails. Running a farm therefore means funding each alias through a waiting period with no reward, which is a capital cost an honest single agent forfeits once and never again. That is 2 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
